title: SHA-1 (block structure)
summary: SHA-1 processes input in 512-bit (64-byte) blocks. Similar to SHA-256 but with 160-bit (20-byte) output. 80 rounds (vs SHA-256's 64). Uses 5 working variables (a-e). Broken for collision resistance (SHAttered attack, 2017). Still used in Git (object IDs), TLS (legacy), and many systems.

structure.meaning: Input chunk, padded to multiple of 64 bytes.
The 16 32-bit words of the message block (big-endian).
Extended words: W[t] = (W[t-3] XOR W[t-8] XOR W[t-14] XOR W[t-16]) <<< 1.
a, b, c, d, e (initial: H0-H4).
4 stages (20 rounds each) with different functions: Ch, Parity, Maj, Parity. K constants per stage.

notes: SHA-1 is broken for collision resistance (SHAttered: 2^63 operations, 2017).
SHA-1 is still used in Git (object IDs), TLS (legacy), and many systems.
Git uses SHA-1 for content addressing. SHA-256 migration (SHA-256 repo format) is in progress.
SHA-1's 160-bit output is shorter than SHA-256's 256-bit, making collisions easier.
